messages.content:
A writer revised their English post sentence by sentence. Compare the version before the revision with the final one, as an editor protecting what the writer meant.

Before:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about it.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest sky, and it would be hard / not worth it to get back here for a distant little kittypet who wants to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear day; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>

Final:
<<<
I’m on the early chapters of Darktail’s Judgment, and I get a little bit confused about why StarClan didn’t show up when Darkpaw was at the moonstone and he got really miserable and furious about it.

Ravenpaw said StarClan had travelled with the Clans and left the forest sky, and it would be too hard to get back here for a little kittypet from far away who wants to join the Clans. But it was mentioned in the book that it was a overcast day, so without the moonlight it makes sense that they couldn’t reach StarClan back then when the Clans were still in the forest. (Could someone tell me if there was a similar case in the other books that the night sky’s cloudy when a cat was at the Moonstone? Or do StarClan have the power to clear the clouds if they want to communicate?)

And Darkpaw didn’t try again on a clear night; he just chose to transform himself into Darktail👿 instead.
>>>

During the revision the writer confirmed what they meant at these places; changes that follow these are intended:
- 「hard / not worth it」→ 作者转述的是导师的意见："hard"表示能力上做不到，"not worth it"表示不值得做，两者含义不同，需要作者自己决定想表达哪一种，否则读者会误解星族没有出现的原因。
- 「a distant little kittypet」→ Darkpaw是来自遥远之地或与猫族无关的小猫。
- 「on a clear day」→ Darkpaw没有在晴朗的夜晚再去月亮石。

List only real problems in the final version: a point, detail, question or condition from before that is gone (lost); a claim whose meaning changed, e.g. a hedge or a hypothetical that became a flat statement (changed); text that appears twice (duplicated); a sentence that is broken where two pieces were joined (broken). Rewording, reordering and better phrasing are not problems. quote: the exact words from the final version (or, for lost, from before); note: one short Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China) sentence to the writer, informal. [] if there is nothing.
Reply with JSON only: {"issues":[{"kind":"lost|changed|duplicated|broken","quote":"","note":""}]}
